Everything is built, wired, and verified. I've switched to **Phase 4 (Acceptance)** and the finished application is now available for you to use at **http://maker:4000**.

**Verification report (plain language):** every approved behaviour was tested and passed — **30 internal tests + 6 end-to-end tests, all green.** That covers: quick saving with in-place review; the saved item with a separate formatted note; searching across address/title/description/note (case-insensitive, with `#tag`, `"phrases"`, `AND/OR/NOT`, parentheses, and the gentle "incomplete query" note); tags with suggestions and match-all filtering; read-later and archive with their own views; permanent delete (guarded, separate from archive); editing the address with uniqueness protection; no-duplicate re-saving with trailing-slash/http-vs-https treated as the same and secure address kept; bulk selection and actions; live saved collections; import/export of the standard bookmarks file; settings for default sort, text size, per-page paging, and auto-copy; and the real-favicon-with-fallback plus preview.

**One honest caveat:** the parts that reach outside — saving a **local page/PDF copy**, creating an **Internet Archive** copy, and fetching the **real favicon/preview** — are fully implemented server-side, but their *online* success couldn't be exercised in the offline test sandbox. Their **graceful-failure paths are verified** (a save still works when a page can't be read; endpoints return clear reasons; the bookmark is never harmed). Please confirm these when you're on a network with outbound access. This is recorded in the verification notes rather than claimed as proven.

Also recorded **for a later cycle** (not in this build): a full backup/restore, an explicit "refresh details from page," and performance tuning for very large collections.

Please try the app at **http://maker:4000**. Then:

**Do you accept this software as implementing the behaviour we approved, completing this cycle?** If anything doesn't match what we approved, tell me and I'll treat it as a fix within this cycle; if it's a new or changed behaviour, I'll record it for the next cycle.
